messages:
maria: heads-up — we're seeing a weird cluster of 413s from the embeddings route when clients send mixed-dim batches after the prefetch console flag landed. seen it in prod canary (1%)

sam: repro snippet? i ran into a few 413s earlier but thought it was client framing.

maria: repro paste below — same payload that works in local but causes router to route to splitter then back with reject. note the request has a mix of 64- and 1536-dim vectors.

sam: ```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"ada-embed-001","input":[{"text":"short","dim":64},{"text":"long doc","dim":1536}]}'
```

laura: quick thought — our splitter assumes payload-size-first then dims-second. mixed dims get quantized into different shard paths and sometimes exceed a per-shard byte budget. that explains 413s (payload too large for chosen shard).

aj: telemetry shows spike in `embed.splitter.rejects` and `embed.route.byte_fill` around the same time as the console prefetch boolean flip. @deploy-bot any rollout metadata?

deploy-bot: canary-flip: prefetch_hint=true rolled to 1% at 2025-11-03T14:22:10Z; rollback not triggered.

nate: is the console flag enabling prefetch caching that augments request size (adds index hints)? if so the effective bytes/req go up.

maria: yes — prefetch sends an extra `prefetch_hint` blob with each request to warm caches. we underestimated how that interacts with mixed-dim splitter.

sam: two quick options: 1) fast-fail mixed-dim+prefetch at ingress with user-facing 400 + friendly console CTA, or 2) change the routing to make dims-primary so small dims don't get packed into a shard with a huge prefetch blob.

laura: UX-wise i prefer option 1 for a short-term fix: clear error + console bubble that suggests a `dim_hint` header. long-term we want dims-primary routing.

aj: telemetry-wise we need an experiment metric: `prefetch.added_bytes_by_dim` and `split_reject_rate_by_dim_combo`. can we add those as ephemeral counters for the canary?

maria: i can add a lightweight counter in the splitter (no schema change) and surface it to the canary dashboard. sam, can you add a small check that records dim combos for rejected payloads (pseudonymized)?

sam: yeah. quick patch idea: record tuple key like `d64:d1536` in s3-ev metrics, capped to 500 samples/min. also add a console hint UI that shows "suggest: send same-dim batches or use multiple requests".

nate: console UX: show estimated cost + token/byte impact of `prefetch_hint` per batch. that should drive adoption of dim-aligned calls.

laura: about error code — we should avoid returning 413 without context. propose payload: 413, body: "mixed-dim payload + prefetch_hint exceeded shard capacity. Suggest header: X-Preferred-Embed-Shape: 64 or use batching param. See Console Suggestions > Embeddings."

aj: agree. also add a telemetry tag `console_suggestion_shown=true` when the UI surfaces the CTA so we can A/B it.

maria: rollout plan: revert prefetch to 0% while we patch? or pause canary rollout and keep flag at 1% until metrics collected?

sam: let's pause increasing the canary. keep at 1% so we can gather samples. i'll open an RFC with patch + quick UI change.

nate: for long-term, engineering decision: prefer dims-first routing by default and only group by bytes when dims are uniform. moving to dims-first reduces tail rejects but might slightly reduce batch fill efficiency. need perf/$$ tradeoff doc.

laura: i'll prototype a console mock that displays: recommended batch size, predicted latency, and estimated token-cost delta if user sends mixed dims vs split requests. should help product decide.

maria: action items: sam -> RFC + splitter metric; laura -> console mock + CTA copy; aj -> add ephemeral telemetry counters; nate -> perf tradeoff doc. i'll own the canary coordination.

sam: filing RFC now: RFC-embed-splitter-dim-first-1711000000 (will link).

aj: logging note: please add `embed.splitter.sample_id` to samples so we can correlate logs -> metrics. small and non-PII.

maria: agreed. thanks all. gonna add a temporary alert: alert if `embed.splitter.reject_rate` > 0.2% on canary.

laura: :thumbsup:

sam: i've added the sample-limited counter PR; putting canary patch link in the RFC.

maria: closing thread for now — will update once we have dashboard samples and RFC link.

(quick reactions: many :eyes: and a couple :bug: in the thread)
